findings.text: assert row == ticker_module.queue_pane_row(document) compares the document's pane string against a second invocation of the same function on the same document; both sides move together, so it holds whatever the renderer does and would survive a regression that made queue_pane_row return an empty string, provided the view still assigns it. It guards only the assignment line, and the independent row content is asserted separately at lines 125-128.

_running counts a pointer whose phase is in RUNNING_PHASES without consulting its classification, while reckon/crew/ticker.py:3216-3225 _in_flight_word reads classification first precisely because a stalled run's pointer phase is still 'working'. A stalled request therefore raises the running count and suppresses the 'nothing is running' fault, which is the state the fault exists to report.

_upstream_plans re-implements the plan-slug-before-# transform that reckon/crew/plan_coordinator.py:83 _plan_token already performs (also reckon/doccheck.py:2405 and reckon/schedule.py:80); no module owns that capability publicly, so this is the fifth private copy rather than an extension of an owner.

the rendered pane row is carried on the queue document, but no ticker or fleet-pane surface reads document['pane'] (git grep over reckon/ finds no consumer outside queue_view.py), so the deliverable's 'the pane renders the four parts' is met only for readers of the served queue document; the fleet pane's single waiting figure is still produced in reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py, which this node's write scope excludes and the manifest records under outside_scope.
